title: Chow's lemma for separated morphisms of finite type over a qcqs base
statement: Let $S$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and $f:X\to S$ a separated morphism of finite type [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Then there exist an integer $n\ge0$, a scheme $X'$, a morphism $\pi:X'\to X$ that is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] and surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism], and an immersion $j:X'\to\mathbf P^n_S$ [def-weil-closed-immersion] into the projective space $\mathbf P^n_S=S\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}$ [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change] such that $p\circ j=f\circ\pi$, where $p:\mathbf P^n_S\to S$ is the projection.

proof.text: Use the proved Scheme.Hom.exists_isClosedImmersion_isSeparated_locallyOfFinitePresentation (01ZJ) to choose a closed immersion i:X -> Y and a separated finite-presentation g:Y -> S with i ≫ g = f. Compactness and quasi-separatedness of X follow from f and the qcqs base.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0202 (lemma-chow-finite-type, line 3071), proof, first paragraph, first sentence (Proposition 01ZJ, separated-closed-in-finite-presentation)

proof.text: Choose the existing Scheme.NoetherianApproximation of S using Scheme.nonempty_noetherianApproximation (01ZA). Its index category is already small and cofiltered; its stages are Noetherian, compact and quasi-separated by the proved approximation instances. Apply Scheme.exists_isPullback_of_finitePresentation_of_isSeparated (01ZM and 01ZQ together) to g to obtain a separated finite-presentation model g₀:Y₀ -> S₀ and a pullback square with Y -> Y₀ and S -> S₀. No directed reindexing or extra limit-existence theorem is needed.
Apply the proved ChowModification for g₀ over its Noetherian base, obtaining the finite coordinate type N, the proper surjective π₀, the immersion j₀, and their equality over S₀.

Form Y′ = pullback π₀ h. Paste its pullback square with the model square to show Y′ is the base change of the Chow modification along S -> S₀. ProjectiveSpace.liftBaseChange supplies jY:Y′ -> P(N;S), and ProjectiveSpace.isPullback_liftBaseChange shows it is a base change of j₀, hence an immersion. The projection Y′ -> Y is proper and surjective by base change.

Form X′ = pullback (Y′ -> Y) i. Its projection π to X is proper and surjective. Its projection to Y′ is a closed immersion, hence the composite j:X′ -> Y′ -> P(N;S) is an immersion. The pullback condition and i ≫ g = f give j ≫ projection = π ≫ f; these equalities are proved by rewriting the two pullback conditions.

Apply lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-finite-coordinates to N and S to obtain a closed immersion k:P(N;S) -> P^n_S over S. The composite j ≫ k is an immersion; associativity and the two equations over S prove the required final equality. This preserves all hypotheses and the original numerical projective-space conclusion.
